Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.

# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Change the image into pencil drawing
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is there image-grounded evidence of any progress toward rendering the content as a pencil drawing, even if the transformation is incomplete?
node.criteria: Pass if the image shows some visible pencil-drawing-style treatment of its content, including an incomplete treatment; fail if sufficient evidence shows no requested transformation has progressed; unknown if evidence is insufficient to determine whether any such progress occurred. Unrelated edits do not count as progress.
node.binding: Assess only visible changes in the supplied image that move its visual content toward a pencil-drawn style; do not infer progress from unrelated changes.

node_traces.evidence: The edited image shows a visible pencil-drawing-style treatment: colors are muted and the food and surrounding objects have sketch-like shading and outlines, indicating progress toward the requested style.

fulfillment: The node’s binding asks whether the image appears as a *completed* pencil drawing, but its criteria make s1 passing sufficient for completion. That shortcut is not supported by the trace: s1 describes a muted, grainy pencil style, while s2 explicitly characterizes the visible sketch treatment as progress. The edited image does show a substantial pencil-like rendering, but the evidence does not establish that the requested transformation is complete; the reference is partial. Repair the typed decision logic so completion requires evidence of the requested style being fully realized, and so visible but incomplete style progress can be distinguished from completion. Do not infer completion merely from preserved content or from either support passing alone. Keep unresolved evidence unknown rather than treating low confidence or variation as proof of absence. There is no transport, schema, or dependency failure here: both supports were queried and valid, so investigate the semantic binding and aggregation rule.
